newsitem.title: USA: Potential witness released in Cosby murder probe.
newsitem.headline: Potential witness released in Cosby murder probe.

text.p: Two men questioned by detectives investigating the murder of entertainer Bill Cosby's son were released after giving no relevant information about the slaying, police said on Tuesday.
The men, one of whom reportedly matched a description of a possible witness to last Thursday's killing, were picked up on Monday night in suburban Torrance.
"One male, the passenger in the vehicle, did not fit the description of either composite. He was interviewed and was released," said Los Angeles police spokesman Commander Tim McBride.

He said the driver of the blue hatchback vehicle that matched one reportedly seen near the crime scene, "fit the description of the witness composite and when interviewed acknowledged to being near the location of the murder scene."
Ennis Cosby was gunned down in the early hours of last Thursday while changing a flat tire near a freeway.
Of the two men questioned, McBride told reporters: "It does not appear they're involved in this crime or have any information of substance to help us."
He said the man, who fit the description of a witness police had sought, was "candid and cooperative," saying he was in the area "to look at the city lights."

McBride said the man did not witness the killing "but later saw a police car. But since he had nothing (further) to offer (investigators) he didn't respond (to the police appeal for witnesses)." The man, who was not identified by police, was released after about five hours.

In a brief interview with local KCBS television, the long-haired, goateed man said: "I didn't really see anything that I thought was relevant. But I just told them everything I seen, like I seen another vehicle in the area. That's about it."
He told the TV station police had taken three pairs of his shoes to compare with sole prints at the crime scene, and had dusted his Volkswagen vehicle for fingerprints.
A woman who saw part of the attack gave police a description of the killer as a white man wearing a knit cap, and that was used to put together a composite drawing.

As the investigation continued, the supermarket tabloid the National Enquirer offered a $100,000 reward for information leading to the arrest and conviction of the killer. And its big rival, the Globe, doubled that, offering $200,000.
Bill Cosby had challenged tabloids to put up the money to help catch the killer, rather than paying money to potential witnesses for stories and potentially undermining the police investigation.

The Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors approved a motion on Tuesday to put up a $12,500 award to help find the killer. It also approved a similar reward in the murder of a teenager killed during a gang fight on a school bus the same day as Ennis Cosby was shot.

In another development, a Los Angeles woman and an alleged accomplice were arrested in New York on charges of attempting to extort $40 million from Bill Cosby in exchange for not telling the media she was his illegitimate daughter. A Cosby spokesman vehemently denied the woman was Cosby's daughter.
There is no evidence the blackmail attempt was related to the murder of Cosby's son, Mary Jo White, the U.S. Attorney for the Southern District of New York, said Monday.
